clue.text: It's not gross to eat with pond inhabitant

indicators.note: something that eats takes another thing inside itself, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a net sum is what is left after deductions, the opposite of gross
W is the standard abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Someone declares that dining alongside creatures from the pond is perfectly acceptable, not disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gross' looks like 'disgusting', but here it is the money term: not gross means net.
explanation.definitionFit: A newt is a small amphibian that lives in and around ponds.

clue.text: Hugo and I at the premiere of African Queen

parts.note: Victor Hugo, the French novelist, so his first name stands for him
taken as written

indicators.note: a premiere is a first showing, so only the opening letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of African

explanation.surface: Hugo and the speaker attend the opening night of the film The African Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African Queen' reads as the film title, but the words split: African supplies one letter and Queen alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria was the British monarch who reigned from 1837 to 1901, a famous queen.

clue.text: Become weary of Green

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to tire or exhaust
second meaning: a bluish-green colour named after the gemstone

explanation.surface: Someone grows tired of a person called Green.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital G makes Green look like a surname; it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to make or become worn out; as a noun it is a gemstone and its pale green shade.

clue.text: 'Restricted flight area manager' used as trivia

indicators.note: the letters are put to use in a new way, rearranged rather than taken in order

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A jokey job title, the sort of thing offered as a quiz question or piece of trivia.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted phrase sounds like an air-traffic job, but the restricted flight area is a large birdcage.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviarist keeps an aviary, an enclosure where birds can fly only within limited space.

clue.text: Presidential candidate loses weight with microchip surgery

indicators.note: losing something means a part is taken away from the candidate's name

parts.note: Hillary Clinton ran for US president, as did Bill
a ton is a unit of weight; it is removed
IC is short for integrated circuit, a microchip

explanation.surface: A slimmed-down presidential hopeful undergoes an operation involving a microchip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surgery' suggests an operation, but in British use a surgery is a doctor's consulting room.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a surgery is the place a doctor sees patients, much the same as a clinic.

clue.text: Refusing to alter one's view cannot be spoken of around wife!

indicators.note: around means the phrase's letters wrap about the single-letter abbreviation

parts.note: something that cannot be said is unsayable
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A stubborn person's opinions on the subject of a wife are too shocking to voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who refuses to change their mind cannot be swayed or persuaded.

clue.text: Nameless wild flower

indicators.note: without a name means the abbreviation for name is dropped from the word

parts.note: wild in the sense of fierce or savage
N is the abbreviation for name; it is removed

explanation.surface: A wild flower whose species nobody can name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild flower' reads as one phrase, but wild is the wordplay and flower alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The violet is a small purple-flowered plant common in woods and hedgerows.

clue.text: Opera house, the last for French city

parts.note: the Met is New York's Metropolitan Opera House
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An opera house is named as the final venue on a French tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last' here is the last letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Metz is a city in the Lorraine region of north-eastern France.

clue.text: Bush envoy opening Republican art venue

indicators.note: an opening is a beginning, so only the first letter of the word before is used

parts.note: the first letter of envoy
R is the standard abbreviation for Republican
the ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts in London

explanation.surface: An envoy of President Bush opens a Republican-backed gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: Bush looks like the American president, but it is a shrub; the ICA is a London arts centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical name for heath or heather, a low evergreen shrub.

clue.text: Name Spike (after farewell) as sweetheart

parts.note: vale is Latin for goodbye
N is the abbreviation for name
a tine is a prong or spike, as on a fork

explanation.surface: Someone nominates a person called Spike as their sweetheart after saying goodbye to another.
explanation.walkthrough: '(after farewell)' places the farewell word before the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A valentine is a lover or sweetheart, the one chosen on St Valentine's Day.

clue.text: Old store of brine that fermented

indicators.note: fermenting churns and transforms a substance, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An old storehouse kept salt water that had begun to ferment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe barn was a medieval barn for storing the tenth of produce paid to the church.

clue.text: Progress easily in Disney zone?

parts.note: Walt Disney, the animation pioneer
Z is the abbreviation for zone

explanation.surface: Is getting through a Disney theme park a breeze?
explanation.definitionFit: To waltz through something is an idiom for doing it with ease.

clue.text: I say Gable's last seen with Garland in Fatal Attraction!

parts.note: Lor! is an old exclamation of surprise, like I say!

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the possessive name before it

parts.note: the last letter of Gable
a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland

explanation.surface: Clark Gable appears with Judy Garland in the film Fatal Attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: Gable and Garland are film stars in the surface; Garland is just a garland of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei was a Rhine siren whose singing lured boatmen to their deaths, a deadly allure.

clue.text: Weapon's look not good

indicators.note: not good means the abbreviation for good is left out of the word

parts.note: a glance is a quick look
G is the abbreviation for good; it is removed

explanation.surface: The appearance of a weapon is judged poor.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long spear carried by a mounted knight.

clue.text: English international lacks energy to run, for the main part

indicators.note: lacking something means one letter is missing from the player's title

parts.note: the Lionesses are the England women's football team
E is the symbol for energy; one is removed
to hare is to run fast

explanation.surface: A tired England player is too drained to run for most of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: The England women's football team is nicknamed the Lionesses, so one player is a Lioness.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion's share is an idiom for the largest portion of something.

clue.text: Glass makes blubber last — weird!

parts.note: to blubber is to cry noisily

indicators.note: something weird is strange and out of its normal form, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone finds it strange that a glass makes whale fat keep longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blubber' looks like whale fat, but it is the verb meaning to weep.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystal is a fine, clear type of glass used for tableware.

clue.text: Unsociable type, single, welcomed by political extremes

indicators.note: being welcomed by means being taken in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the extremes of politics are left and right, L and R
single means one

explanation.surface: A solitary, unsociable figure finds favour with the far left and far right.
explanation.definitionFit: A loner is a person who prefers to be alone and avoids company.

clue.text: Marsh transformed in Goa?

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: the five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Has a wetland in the Indian state of Goa been changed?
explanation.walkthrough: Marsh is not wet ground but the crime novelist Ngaio Marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Ngaio Marsh was a New Zealand detective novelist, so her first name stands for the surname.

clue.text: Bell, British soldier: well out of it

indicators.note: out of it means removed from the word just named

parts.note: Tommy is the traditional nickname for a British private soldier
My! and Well! are both exclamations of surprise; it is removed

explanation.surface: A soldier named Bell is drunk or dazed, well out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well out of it' sounds like being dazed; well is the exclamation My.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Tom is the famous bell of Christ Church, Oxford, so Tom names a bell.

clue.text: Drug referee outside college

indicators.note: outside means the verb's letters go round the abbreviation for college

parts.note: to referee a dispute is to mediate
C is the abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: A sports official is caught taking drugs off campus.
explanation.walkthrough: Drug and referee look like nouns but both are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: To medicate someone is to give them a drug or medicine.

clue.text: Stop working for an aristocrat

parts.note: to bar is to stop or prevent
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: An instruction to cease toiling on behalf of a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is a member of the lowest rank of the British peerage, a nobleman.

clue.text: A flavouring of wine: tip of pear in blossom

parts.note: rosé is a pink wine

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the word for blossom

parts.note: may is hawthorn blossom

indicators.note: the tip is the end point, so only the final letter of the fruit is used

parts.note: the last letter of pear

explanation.surface: A wine is flavoured with a hint of pear among the blossom.
explanation.walkthrough: May, the hawthorn blossom, is common in British cryptics; it takes the letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is an aromatic herb widely used to flavour food.

clue.text: In torment, as I survey columnar distortion

indicators.note: In says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: Someone surveys a scene while suffering agony.
explanation.definitionFit: Entasis is the slight outward curve built into a column so it does not look concave.

clue.text: Long time with artist

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
Damien Hirst, the British artist

explanation.surface: A lengthy stretch of time spent in an artist's company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long time' looks like one phrase; Long is the verb meaning to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To thirst for something is to long for it, to crave it.

clue.text: Herb's sort of horse

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sour-leaved salad herb
second meaning: a horse with a reddish-brown coat

explanation.surface: A man called Herb owns a horse of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Herb reads as a man's name with a possessive; the 's means is.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a leafy herb with sharp-tasting leaves and a chestnut-coloured horse.

clue.text: Actor's assistant of no use in a strip club?

definitions.text: Actor's assistant of no use in a strip club?

parts.note: the plain reading: a theatre helper who looks after an actor's costumes

parts.words: of no use in a strip club?
parts.note: the setter's joke: strippers take clothes off, so a helper who puts them on is redundant

explanation.walkthrough: Theatre helpers get actors into costume; in a strip club the point is getting out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre, the person who helps actors into their costumes is called by this name.

clue.text: Trust it to enter note

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the short word sits within the note's name

parts.note: fah is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to rely on a message getting into a written note.
explanation.definitionFit: Faith is complete trust or confidence in someone or something.

clue.text: Supporting duke's cross

parts.note: if you are for something you support it
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: Backing the duke's angry mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry, but it is the verb to cross a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To ford a river is to cross it at a shallow place on foot or by vehicle.

clue.text: Miracle worked — Sheeran's won from evil!

indicators.note: worked means shaped or kneaded, so these letters are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: these letters are rearranged
Ed Sheeran, the British singer-songwriter

explanation.surface: A miracle has happened: the pop star has been saved from wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim someone is to rescue them from a sinful or wasted way of life.

clue.text: Sly has stiffener — way to go

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a curved structure you pass under, an archway

explanation.surface: A crafty person has something to stiffen their resolve and is ready to set off.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle words point the same way: an arch is a stiffening support, as in the arch of a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means slyly playful as an adjective and, as a noun, a curved opening or archway to pass through.

clue.text: Drink taken after entrance to Death Valley

indicators.note: taken after places the drink behind the other piece in the sequence
an entrance is the way in, so only the first letter of the word after is used

parts.note: the first letter of Death
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A drink consumed after arriving at Death Valley in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Death Valley' reads as the desert; Death gives one letter and Valley alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dale is a valley, especially in northern England.

clue.text: Inject new life into right sort of rest cure

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: sort means to arrange, so the following letters are put into a different order

parts.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A proper rest cure revives a tired person.
explanation.definitionFit: To resurrect something is to bring it back to life or revive it.

clue.text: Two sides missing from Lewis's song

indicators.note: missing from means those letters are absent from the author's name

parts.note: the two sides are right and left, R and L; one of each is removed
Lewis Carroll, author of Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A song by Lewis has lost both its sides.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll's surname is meant; dropping one R and one L leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A carol is a song, especially a festive Christmas hymn.
